title: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina (II)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was the student of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, as in Sanhedrin 29a, where he said: “From the lecture of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba I heard that the inciter is different.” In Berakhot 5b: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said that Rabbi Yitzchak said.” Hyman quotes Sukkah 47a: “Rabbi Yochanan said: One does not say the time-blessing on the eighth day of the festival … Rabbi Levi bar Chama — and some say Rabbi Chama bar Chanina — said: Know.” He was the colleague of Rabbi Chelbo, as in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3, folio 32a, where they disagree; and he disagrees with Rabbi Yissakhar of Kefar Mandi, Bereshit Rabbah 52:5 and 74:7 and Vayikra Rabbah 1:13.

For the most part we find him only in aggadah, as in Berakhot 15b, where he said: “Whoever recites the Shema and pronounces its letters precisely — Gehinnom is cooled for him.” “Why are tents placed next to streams?” etc. There, 32b: “If a person sees that he prayed and was not answered, he should pray again, as it is said, ‘Hope,’” etc. There, 56b: “What is the verse? ‘I will go down.’” Hyman cites Shabbat 10b: “One who gives a gift to his fellow must inform him.” Yoma 28b: “From the days of our forefathers, the academy never departed from them.” Taanit 7a: “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘Iron sharpens iron’? Just as with iron, one sharpens the other, so two Torah scholars sharpen each other in halakhah.” Sotah 13b: “From Shechem they stole him (Joseph), and to Shechem we shall return what was lost [his remains].” “Whoever does something and does not finish it, and another comes and finishes it, Scripture credits it to the one who finished it.” “Why did Joseph die before his brothers? Because he conducted himself with authority.” There, 14a: “Even Moses our teacher does not know where he is buried … Why was Moses buried near Beit Pe’or?” etc. In Kiddushin 70b: “When the Holy One, blessed be He, rests His presence, He rests it only on families of distinguished lineage in Israel … When the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies the tribes, He purifies the tribe of Levi first.” In Sanhedrin 8a: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Is it not enough for the wicked that they take money from this one,” etc. There, 35a: “From where are these words? Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: For the verse says, ‘full of justice’ … Rava said,” etc.

We likewise find his homilies in Bereshit Rabbah 47:2, 67:1–2 and 75:9; Shemot Rabbah 1:9, 1:25 and 8:2; Eichah Rabbah 2:10 and beginning of chapter 3; Tanchuma, Vayechi 6, Va’era 8, Beshalach 23, Mishpatim 10, Shoftim 6 and 9; Midrash Tehillim 78:2; and Midrash Mishlei 12:20, 20:2, 25:1 and 31:10. Of those who speak in his name we find Rabbi Levi bar Chama, as in Rosh Hashanah 29b and Zevachim 53b.

Rabbi Pinchas and Rabbi Acha in his name: Midrash Tehillim 40:4. Hyman infers from this that this Rabbi Chama bar Chanina is Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa, cited in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 6, on the verse “Turn your eyes,” where Rabbi Pinchas spoke in his name.
In Midrash Tehillim 40:4 we find him with Rabbi Yudan and Rabbi Idi.

notes.text: שאני מסית is the inciter is different, not that it is an inciter; אצל is near, not opposite. Hyman’s Sukkah47a NEGATIVE time-blessing statement stays supplied, alongside the returned Gemara’s POSITIVE eighth-day statement and negative seventh-day-Pesach clause. The supplied Mishlei פ״ף־ב cannot be safely converted to20:2; retain it literally and hold p003. מדדין is read מחדדין. His Chanina barPappa filiation remains a proposal.

שאני מסית means that the inciter is different, rather than “that it is an inciter”; אצל in the Moses burial question is “near,” rather than “opposite.” The supplied Sukkah 47a quotation says not to recite the time-blessing on the eighth festival day. The saved Davidson text instead says to recite it on that day and not on the seventh day of Pesach. Both propositions remain distinct; the supplied negation is not removed.

Taanit 7a, Davidson edition, quotes ברזל בברזל יחד and immediately explains the sharpening comparison; the verse is rendered “Iron sharpens iron.” The supplied מדדין is read contextually as מחדדין. Sotah 13b places the Shechem saying in the context of Joseph’s burial: “what was lost [his remains]” makes that referent explicit without changing the destination or theft claim.

The supplied Mishlei locator is פ״ף־ב. A fresh check of the named Buber Midrash Mishlei 20:2 finds Rabbi Chama bar Chanina in the exposition of “The king’s terror is like a lion’s growl.” The English retains the supplied פ״ף־ב alongside Buber 20:2 as a named-edition comparison; no Hyman printed-letter or correction-history proof is claimed.
The proposed identification with Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa remains Hyman’s inference from the reporting chain, rather than an established genealogy.

The earlier notes record the review before the printed page was checked. Hyman’s London edition (vol. II, p. 461) prints פ״ך־ב, chapter 20, section 2. The supplied transcription gives פ״ף־ב. In Buber’s Midrash Mishlei 20:2, Rabbi Chama bar Chanina compares the fear at a lion cub’s roar with the fear at God’s roar. The translation follows the printed reference, and the supplied Hebrew remains as transcribed.

Hyman’s print also has the negative wording in the quotation from Sukkah 47a. The consulted text affirms the blessing on the eighth day of Sukkot and omits it on the seventh day of Pesach. In Shabbat 10b, Rava bar Mechasya cites Rav Chama bar Gurya in Rav’s name for the duty to tell the recipient about a gift. The same passage quotes Rav Chama bar Chanina saying there is no need to tell the recipient when the gift is likely to become known.

In the consulted Berakhot 5b, the Hebrew reads “Chama son of Rabbi Chanina,” while the English treats Rabbi Chanina as an additional speaker in the chain. Sanhedrin 35a attributes “full of justice” to Rabbi Chanina. Rosh Hashanah 29b reads Levi bar Lachma, whereas Zevachim 53b reads Levi bar Chama. Hyman’s text at these points is reflected in the translation.

In Buber’s Midrash Tehillim 40:4, Rabbi Yudan, Rabbi Idi and Rabbi Chama bar Chanina transmit a teaching from an elder in Rabbi’s name. Another consulted text gives Yudan, Addi and Chama in a chain ending with Rabbi Levi. Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:5 gives Rabbi Pinchas in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina bar Pappa. The identification and the Pinchas and Acha attribution to Midrash Tehillim remain Hyman’s account.
